headline: Indian Markets Face Black Monday Crash Fears Amid Global AI Selloff Concerns

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Fears of a Black Monday crash have gripped Indian stock markets amid weak global cues.
A global AI-driven tech selloff and Nasdaq weakness are weighing on broader investor sentiment.
Gold recovered from a 14-month low as investors turn attention to upcoming US inflation data.
Markets are evaluating recent strong FII buying against fresh global market volatility.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty hit 9-month highs recently following a 4-week rally supported by record FII buying.
Noel Tata requested to defer the Tata Sons board meeting scheduled for November 26.
Asian markets faced pressure as South Korean shares slumped nearly 3% on AI tech selloffs.
Investors are tracking market schedule updates with Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday falling on November 24.
summary: Indian stock markets enter trading today under the shadow of global AI tech selloffs and Black Monday crash fears. This comes right after Sensex and Nifty climbed to 9-month highs following a robust four-week rally fueled by record FII inflows. Traders are closely monitoring global market cues and upcoming US inflation data.
